terms.grammar: irregular verb, with the dative: sē perīculīs offerre
evidence: Cic. Off. 1.83: nē offerāmus nōs perīculīs sine causā (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of exposing oneself, willingly, to danger or death. Its everyday sense is to offer or present.

terms.gloss: expose, put in the way of
terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation (-iō), with the dative
terms.comment: To throw or put something in front of someone or something, and so to expose to danger. It also means to throw something to someone (food to a dog: Verg. A. 6.421) and to reproach someone with something (objicere alicui aliquid).

evidence: Caes. B.G. 2.6: mūrus dēfēnsōribus nūdātus (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Properly to strip or bare; in war, to leave a place without defenders.

phrases.latin: nē offerāmus nōs perīculīs sine causā
phrases.english: let us not expose ourselves to danger without good reason

sources: Lewis & Short: offero · Lewis & Short: obicio · Lewis & Short: nudo
